product: AltContext customer account portal (APP-1) — standalone React/Vite SPA at apps/app-portal
goals: OBSERVED-UI account chrome: visible sign-in, sign-up, signed-in user chrome, and sign-out. @clerk/react SignIn/SignUp own the credential forms; this app does not invent a password field (NAV-08, NAV-12, CARD-06).

Disabled/unavailable configuration is a designed screen, not a blank shell: missing VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, portal flag off, or Clerk session load failure each have copy and no primary auth action (RLSE-04, CARD-03, FORM-09).

No fake tenant claims: Clerk user id/email is identity only. Tenant UUID, admission, and API keys remain existing backend authority. Never render Clerk OrganizationSwitcher or a guessed tenant name (DOM-03, CARD-12, HAI-05).
Never put CLERK_SECRET_KEY in the browser. Publishable key only. Wrap Clerk behind the SPA auth chrome so the rest of the product can swap identity later (REF-15, CARD-16).
Logout is a first-class exit back to signed-out chrome. Signed-in-but-not-admitted is a distinct error, not a tenant dashboard (NAV-07, CARD-15).

B0 browser-fix invariants are frozen before B1: account state is keyed by Clerk session/user, private account reads are no-store and bounded with token refresh, signed-in backend outage keeps UserButton and Sign out, a 200 /portal/me payload without a valid tenant_id is invalid data rather than an unlinked tenant, and unadmitted access is backend 403 (RLSE-04, NAV-11, HAI-01).

B1 planned journeys remain in this map: verified-identity invitation claim, tenant API-key lifecycle and one-time secret handling, honest usage, WordPress Test Connection guidance, and billing checkout/manage recovery. These are offline planning contracts, not live provider evidence.

jobs.label: Sign in or sign up with Clerk and return to the account origin
See the signed-in Clerk user and sign out
Understand when the portal cannot run and what to do next
Redeem one verified invitation into the backend-owned tenant binding
Create, list, rotate, revoke, and safely copy tenant API credentials
Read bounded usage and entitlement evidence without invented counts
Start or recover hosted billing without granting access from a redirect

screens.title: Account › Signed in

UserButton shows the signed-in person and Sign out is visible. open-user-menu is available in signed-in default/loading chrome; sign-out remains the session exit. Tenant/key/billing regions stay withheld until backend /portal/me supplies a valid tenant binding; a 200 payload without a valid tenant_id is invalid backend data, not an unlinked tenant label. Never invent a tenant from Clerk org or email local-part (DOM-03, CARD-12). loading is the Clerk plus backend identity check. error is backend 401 session verification failure with retry. Backend 403 not_admitted routes to portal-not-admitted; backend outage routes to portal-backend-outage while preserving UserButton and Sign out (RLSE-04, NAV-11, HAI-01). Serves manage-session.

Keep the signed-in UserButton and Sign out reachable; retry only the account read. Do not manufacture a tenant, key, usage, or billing state (RLSE-04, NAV-11, HAI-01). Serves recover-unavailable.

zones.label: PLANNED-UI: Account access is temporarily unavailable. Try again. Do not expose 503 detail text or claim that keys/usage are lost.
PLANNED-UI B0-fix: UserButton and Sign out remain visible while retrying the backend identity read; session exit is independent of the outage.

screens.title: Onboarding › Claim invitation
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI verified-identity claim. A signed-in Clerk person with a verified, non-empty email may enter one invitation_token to POST /portal/onboarding/claim before a tenant exists. The final single-use mutation stays behind a preview/confirmation; the browser never selects tenant_id, stores the raw token, or calls Polar. First success is 201 with replayed false; the same bound identity may receive 200 replayed true. Backend keeps unknown, expired, or email-mismatched invitations non-enumerating as 403 not_admitted. Serves claim-tenant-access (DOM-03, HAI-01).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI: show verified Clerk identity context only. Missing/unverified email is backend 403 email_unverified; no tenant selector and no account claim from email local-part.

PLANNED-UI form: invitation_token is entered or pasted into memory for one request only. Never place it in a URL, localStorage, sessionStorage, logs, analytics, or copied status text. Show a readable preview/confirmation before the single-use mutation; loading disables submit and preserves focus.

PLANNED-UI exact backend vocabulary: 201/200 success with replayed; 401 invalid_portal_authorization; 403 email_unverified, not_admitted, tenant_header_forbidden, csrf_origin_denied; 409 invitation_consumed or identity_already_bound; 422 invalid_claim_request; 503 portal_identity_unavailable. UI gives recovery without revealing which invitation check failed.

screens.title: Developer access › API keys
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI tenant-bound API-key lifecycle. GET /portal/keys returns bounded metadata including revoked history, never hashes or raw secrets. Create and rotate return a raw_key only on the first successful non-replayed response; list, GET, and replay responses never reveal it. Revoke is immediate and requires a destructive confirmation when it is the last usable key. Serves manage-api-keys (NAV-11, HAI-01, RLSE-04).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI list: id, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, rate_limit_tier, lifetime_seconds, and tenant_id metadata only. Cursor paging is bounded (default 25, max 100); expired and revoked rows are visibly different from usable rows.

PLANNED-UI actions: Create when no usable key exists; Rotate only the current primary usable key; Revoke from a confirmation dialog. Create/rotate use an Idempotency-Key and retry by replay, not by minting a second secret.

PLANNED-UI last-key warning: a 409 detail.code last_usable_key_confirmation_required names confirmation_field confirm_last_usable. Show the consequence before Revoke; do not silently send emergency=true.

PLANNED-UI guidance link: after a secret is copied, explain that WordPress Test Connection is a separate plugin evidence step. No current portal.py route is claimed for that test, and the raw secret is not sent back to this portal.

screens.title: Developer access › One-time API secret
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI one-time secret dialog after create or rotate. raw_key is available only in the non-replayed issue response; a replay has raw_key null. Copy and close are explicit. Closing clears the in-memory secret and returns focus to the initiating Create or Rotate control. Copy failure is recoverable without a second API request (CARD-15, RLSE-04).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI secret value: render only from the current response in memory; no URL, storage, analytics, log, or later fetch. Never show a replayed response as if it contained a new secret.

PLANNED-UI primary Copy secret and secondary Close. On copy success show copied status; on clipboard error keep the dialog open with a retry/copy instruction. Close clears the value and restores focus to the source row action.

screens.title: Developer access › WordPress Test Connection
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI handoff guidance, not a claimed API. Explain that the copied API secret is pasted into the WordPress plugin's configured API-key field, then the plugin's Test Connection control provides the WordPress-side result. The portal does not receive the secret back. Exact live menu labels, plugin version behavior, and error copy require later WordPress evidence.

zones.label: PLANNED-UI: 1) copy the secret once, 2) paste it into the WordPress plugin, 3) run Test Connection there, 4) return here to rotate or revoke if needed. Do not paste the secret into chat, screenshots, URLs, or support tickets.

PLANNED-UI recovery: if WordPress reports an auth, expiry, or connectivity failure, return to the key row and inspect metadata or rotate; do not assume a billing or Clerk outage. Live WordPress proof is later evidence.

screens.title: Account › Usage
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI honest usage read. GET /portal/usage is tenant-bound and returns nullable used/reserved/remaining/allowance, required period bounds, optional as_of/status, and data_source. The browser displays backend remaining; it never computes entitlement or converts missing evidence into zero. Distinguish authoritative, pending/unknown, expired, cap reached, past_due grace, and 503 outage. Serves read-usage (HAI-01, RLSE-04).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI summary: show used, reserved, remaining, allowance only when each field is present; show period_start/period_end and as_of when present. data_source is evidence context, not a price or entitlement guess.

PLANNED-UI state copy: unknown when counts are null; pending when data_source is pending; expired when status=expired; cap reached only when backend remaining=0; past_due retains only backend-authorized grace; outage on 503 with Try again. Never client-compute remaining.

screens.title: Account › Billing
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI billing entry. Checkout and manage are tenant-bound POST routes requiring Origin and server-selected relative return paths. Continue to checkout creates or replays a hosted checkout attempt and opens provider navigation; it does not charge by itself, so the action is reversible until authoritative billing state changes. payments_enabled defaults false, so disabled is an honest first state. The UI may submit only a configured public plan_code; there is no current catalog route for prices or product IDs, so it must not fabricate price, currency, or plan entitlements. Serves manage-billing (NAV-11, HAI-01).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI catalog boundary: render only a coordinator-provided configured public plan_code when one exists. No ad-hoc price, product ID, currency, or client entitlement calculation. If the catalog is empty or payments are disabled, show that honestly.

PLANNED-UI checkout: POST /portal/billing/checkout with Origin, Authorization, Idempotency-Key, plan_code, and optional relative return_path. 200 may be pending/provider_requested/succeeded; checkout_url null on succeeded replay. This creates or replays hosted navigation and does not charge by itself; the external redirect is never proof of paid access.

PLANNED-UI manage: POST /portal/billing/manage opens the hosted customer portal only when a mapping exists. 409 billing_customer_missing is a recoverable setup state; 503 billing_portal_unavailable gets retry. Manage cannot change tenant or grant entitlement.

PLANNED-UI exact codes: payments_disabled, csrf_origin_denied, unknown_plan_code, invalid_return_path, invalid_idempotency_key, idempotency_key_reuse, checkout_ambiguous, already_subscribed, checkout_unavailable, billing_customer_missing, billing_portal_unavailable. Preserve attempt_id and Retry-After when provided.

screens.title: Account › Billing return
screens.purpose: PLANNED-UI return landing for /billing/return and /billing/cancel. A provider redirect can show pending, canceled, expired, or recovery copy, but never grants paid access. Paid state is shown only after an authoritative billing projection/usage read reports it. Preserve focus on the billing status panel when returning from an external tab or hosted portal (RLSE-04, NAV-11).

zones.label: PLANNED-UI: status panel announces pending reconciliation until backend evidence changes; success URL is not a paid grant. checkout_ambiguous keeps the same attempt_id and tells the user not to create another checkout.

PLANNED-UI primary Return to billing restores focus to the checkout/manage region. Cancel or expired attempts may start a new purchase only with a new durable attempt and idempotency key; no automatic duplicate redirect.

Does not revoke tenant API keys (backend authority) (RLSE-04, CARD-15). Serves manage-session.

zones.label: OBSERVED-UI: Session ended. Browser returns to signed-out chrome. Existing API keys are unchanged.
OBSERVED-UI: Signing out. Tenant/account fetch data already cleared. No key-revoke copy.
OBSERVED-UI: Sign out failed. Account data stays cleared. Try again retries sign-out (NAV-07, RLSE-04).

open_questions: Resolved for this slice: routed @clerk/react <SignIn /> and <SignUp /> on /sign-in and /sign-up with app chrome doors. Hosted Account Portal buttons are not used.
Resolved for this slice: missing VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is client-detectable; VITE_PORTAL_ENABLED is the public build-time flag; Clerk outage is a bounded wait then retry. Never CLERK_SECRET_KEY.

B1 claim boundary: the invitation token is entered only on the dedicated claim screen after verified identity; it is hashed and consumed by the backend transaction, not treated as a Clerk credential or tenant selector.

B1 catalog boundary: no GET plan-catalog route is present in current portal.py. UI may use only an explicitly configured public plan_code; price, currency, product id, and entitlement remain server/provider authority.
B1 WordPress boundary: targeted current plugin source did not provide a Test Connection UI/API anchor. Guidance is mapped, but exact live labels and success/error evidence remain later acceptance.
not_doing: Do not scaffold Clerk over the monorepo root or the WordPress plugin. SPA lives only in apps/app-portal.
Do not use Next.js Clerk APIs (@clerk/nextjs, auth(), clerkMiddleware). Package is @clerk/react.
Do not put CLERK_SECRET_KEY, webhook secrets, or login material in the SPA, commits, or this map.
Do not render OrganizationSwitcher, fake tenant names, or treat Clerk email as tenant UUID (DOM-03).
Do not put API-key hashes or raw secrets in the browser outside the one-time in-memory issue dialog; list/read responses are metadata only and revoke remains a destructive backend mutation.
Do not compute entitlement, remaining usage, plan price, or paid state in the client. Display nullable usage and authoritative status/data_source from backend responses.
Do not grant paid access from a billing redirect, invent a catalog item, or retry an ambiguous checkout as a new attempt.
Do not claim WordPress Test Connection, production Clerk, Polar sandbox, or provider webhook evidence from offline doubles.
Do not claim live Clerk, Polar, or Caddy CSP policy from this offline SPA slice.
Do not replace local API-key recognition when sign-in is down; this SPA failure is portal-only (CARD-16, REF-15).

Do not run CLI init, accountless setup, login, provisioning, or credential-file access for this offline slice. Use manual @clerk/react integration with offline mocks; do not hardcode a rescued app ID as proof of the production application.
Do not add a second uxmap file: B1 extends app-portal.uxmap.json and preserves every existing B0 id.
